subject: Art & Design
title: Type Scale: Building a Harmonious System
description: A quick win: understand Type Scale: Building a Harmonious System.

hook.text: Random font sizes — 13px, 17px, 22px, 31px — feel chaotic. A type scale brings order.

buildup.text: A type scale is a set of sizes related by a consistent ratio, like musical intervals.

discovery.text: The 'major third' scale (ratio 1.25) is popular: 16, 20, 25, 31.25. Each step feels naturally bigger.

twist.text: You don't need many sizes. Most designs work beautifully with just 5-7 scale steps.

climax.text: Design systems like Material and IBM Carbon publish their type scales for anyone to use.

punchline.text: Pick a ratio. Trust the math. Let the scale do the work.

quiz.question: What is a type scale?
options: A set of font sizes related by a consistent mathematical ratio
The maximum size a font can reach

details.summary: A type scale is a predefined set of font sizes that creates visual harmony through mathematical relationships — typically based on ratios like 1.25 (Major Third), 1.333 (Perfect Fourth), or 1.618 (Golden Ratio). Using a scale instead of arbitrary sizes ensures consistent, proportional hierarchy.
details.whyItMatters: Arbitrary font sizes create inconsistent designs that feel off without viewers knowing why. A mathematical type scale brings the same harmony to text sizing that musical scales bring to pitch, creating designs that feel inherently balanced.
takeaways: Type scales use mathematical ratios for harmonious sizing
Common ratios include Major Third (1.25) and Perfect Fourth (1.333)
Scales replace arbitrary sizes with consistent proportions

faq.question: How do you choose which ratio to use?
faq.answer: Smaller ratios (1.125, 1.2) produce subtle differences suited for mobile and content-heavy designs. Larger ratios (1.414, 1.618) produce dramatic differences suited for marketing pages and editorial design.

faq.question: What is a practical type scale for the web?
faq.answer: A popular scale based on a 16px base with a 1.25 ratio: 12px, 14px, 16px (base), 20px, 25px, 31px, 39px. Tools like typescale.com generate scales visually. Design systems like Material Design provide pre-built scales that have been tested across thousands of applications.
